U3-D-23Month-end fee batch with per-account SAVEPOINTs (real-world)L5Executable

A fee of 900 is charged to each of 101, 102, 103, 104. Each posting is two statements: insert into u3_fee_log, then debit the account. A failed posting must be fully undone without losing the others.

START TRANSACTION;
SAVEPOINT sp_101;
INSERT INTO u3_fee_log VALUES (101, 900);
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 900 WHERE acc_no = 101;   -- ok

SAVEPOINT sp_102;
INSERT INTO u3_fee_log VALUES (102, 900);
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 900 WHERE acc_no = 102;   -- ok

SAVEPOINT sp_103;
INSERT INTO u3_fee_log VALUES (103, 900);
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 900 WHERE acc_no = 103;   -- ok

SAVEPOINT sp_104;
INSERT INTO u3_fee_log VALUES (104, 900);                           -- ok
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 900 WHERE acc_no = 104;
-- ERROR 3819: Check constraint 'chk_bal' is violated.
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_104;      -- removes the log row for 104
COMMIT;
Expected. Fee-log rows for 101, 102 and 103 only; balances 9100, 4100, 19100, 800. The failed posting for 104 is the only thing undone. The ROLLBACK TO is what removes 104's log row, because the failed UPDATE rolled back only its own statement.
Oracle: one anonymous block looping over the accounts with an inner BEGIN … EXCEPTION WHEN OTHERS THEN ROLLBACK TO sp_posting; END;. Re-issuing SAVEPOINT sp_posting moves the earlier savepoint of that name, which is why the loop works.
U3-D-25Shadow paging — crash during the commit sequenceL4Manual

Committed table: P1→L1 (10), P2→L2 (20), P3→L3 (30). T sets P1 = 11 (copied to L4) and P2 = 21 (copied to L5). Commit has three steps: (1) write the current page table to disk, (2) update the root pointer to the new table, (3) free the old locations L1 and L2.

Crash pointState after restartUnreachable locations
(i) before step 1P1→L1=10, P2→L2=20, P3→L3=30L4, L5 (reclaimed)
(ii) after step 1, before step 2same as (i) — the root still points to the old tableL4, L5 (the new table on disk is unused)
(iii) after step 2, before step 3P1→L4=11, P2→L5=21, P3→L3=30L1, L2 (garbage not on the free list)
Recovery rule: the database uses whichever page table the root pointer designates. Atomicity follows from step 2 being a single pointer write — the transaction is either entirely visible or entirely absent. In case (iii) a restart scan (or garbage collection) finds the locations not referenced by the active table and frees them.

Part 4 — Essential SQL Reference

A compact, copy-ready reference. Side-by-side differences are marked. All MySQL syntax is 8.0; Oracle is 12c+ unless a version note says otherwise.

Compatibility flags used throughout

MySQL: enforced CHECK needs 8.0.16+ · EXPLAIN ANALYZE 8.0.18+ · EXPLAIN FORMAT=TREE 8.0.16+ · FOR UPDATE NOWAIT / SKIP LOCKED 8.0.1+ · performance_schema.data_locks 8.0.1+.
Oracle: identity columns and FETCH FIRST need 12c+.

1.Transaction Control

ActionMySQLOracle
Begin a transactionSTART TRANSACTION;Implicit at first DML; optionally SET TRANSACTION READ WRITE;
CommitCOMMIT;COMMIT;
Roll backROLLBACK;ROLLBACK;
SavepointSAVEPOINT s1;SAVEPOINT s1;
Partial rollbackROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT s1;ROLLBACK TO s1;
AutocommitSET autocommit = 0|1;SET AUTOCOMMIT ON|OFF; (client setting)
Isolation levelSET SESSION TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL SERIALIZABLE;
Row count affectedSELECT ROW_COUNT();SQL%ROWCOUNT (inside PL/SQL)
 
-- Canonical transfer (reset script first: UPDATE u3_account …; COMMIT;)
-- MySQL
START TRANSACTION;
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 2000 WHERE acc_no = 101;
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance + 2000 WHERE acc_no = 102;
COMMIT;

-- Oracle: the same without START TRANSACTION (a transaction starts at the first DML)
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 2000 WHERE acc_no = 101;
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance + 2000 WHERE acc_no = 102;
COMMIT;
Two rules that decide most transaction exercises
  • DDL commits implicitly in both databases — a later ROLLBACK undoes nothing (U3-D-02).
  • A failed statement rolls back only itself; the transaction stays open, so an explicit ROLLBACK/COMMIT is still required (U3-B-04, U3-C-23, U3-D-01).

2.Locking

LockMySQLOracle
Exclusive row lock (read for update)SELECT … WHERE … FOR UPDATE;SELECT … WHERE … FOR UPDATE;
Shared row lockSELECT … FOR SHARE;Row reads take no lock; use LOCK TABLE … IN SHARE MODE;
No waitFOR UPDATE NOWAIT (error 3572)FOR UPDATE NOWAIT (ORA-00054)
Timed waitSET innodb_lock_wait_timeout = 3;FOR UPDATE WAIT 3; (ORA-30006)
Skip locked rowsFOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKEDFOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED
Observe locksperformance_schema.data_locksv$lock (needs privileges)
Deadlock errorERROR 1213 (40001)ORA-00060
 
-- MySQL: read a row exclusively, so a second session blocks (the classic lost-update fix)
START TRANSACTION;
SELECT balance FROM u3_account WHERE acc_no = 101 FOR UPDATE;
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 1000 WHERE acc_no = 101;
COMMIT;

-- MySQL: book the first free seat without racing another session
SELECT seat_no FROM u3_seat WHERE train_no=12001 AND status='FREE'
  ORDER BY seat_no LIMIT 1 FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED;
Oracle restriction worth memorising

Oracle does not allow a row-limiting clause (FETCH FIRST) together with FOR UPDATE. Use a per-row FOR UPDATE NOWAIT loop instead (U3-B-08).

PurposeMySQLOracle

-- Transaction failure recovery, MySQL (the only "recovery" both engines expose to SQL)
START TRANSACTION;
SAVEPOINT sp_104;
INSERT INTO u3_fee_log VALUES (104, 900);
UPDATE u3_account SET balance = balance - 900 WHERE acc_no = 104;
-- ERROR 3819: Check constraint 'chk_bal' is violated.
ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT sp_104;      -- undo this posting only
COMMIT;                            -- keep the earlier postings
What SQL cannot do

Neither engine exposes deferred modification, shadow paging, a manual UNDO/REDO pass or a 2PL/TO/OCC scheduler switch. Those exercises (C-11 to C-17, C-21, C-22, C-24 to C-29, D-05 to D-22, D-24 to D-27) are paper simulations — the SQL half only shows the effects of the recovery machinery.

Part 5 — Last-Minute Revision

Everything you need in the final hour: the definitions, the formulas, the differences, the rules and the traps, plus a priority list of question IDs.

1.Ten Definitions You Must Be Able to State

TermOne-line definition
Query treeA diagram of a relational-algebra expression: leaves are relations, internal nodes are operators, the root is the result.
SelectivityThe fraction of tuples satisfying a predicate; result size = input tuples × selectivity.
TransactionA logical unit of work that is either entirely committed or entirely rolled back.
ACIDAtomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
ConflictTwo operations on the same item from different transactions where at least one is a write.
Conflict serializableThe precedence graph is acyclic.
RecoverableIf Tj reads from Ti, then Ti commits before Tj.
Strict 2PLAll exclusive locks are held until commit/abort — gives serializability and strictness.
Write-ahead loggingThe log record for a change reaches stable storage before the changed page does.
CheckpointA point where all log records and modified pages are forced to disk, bounding how far recovery must scan.

2.Formulas on One Screen

FormulaUse
bf = ⌊B / t⌋  ·  b = ⌈n / bf⌉Blocking factor and block count of a relation
|result| = n × s₁ × s₂ × …Result cardinality with independent predicates
Cost_BNL = b_o + ⌈b_o/(M−2)⌉ × b_iBlock nested-loop join (put the smaller relation outer)
Cost_INL = b_o + n_o × (h + k)Index nested-loop join
Scan = b  ·  Clustered = h + ⌈r/bf⌉  ·  Secondary = h + rAccess-path costs for a single-table selection
Break-even: h + r = b → r = b − hWhere the scan beats a secondary index
Read: abort if TS(T) < W-TS(X)Basic timestamp ordering — read rule
Write: abort if TS(T) < R-TS(X) or TS(T) < W-TS(X)Basic timestamp ordering — write rule
Thomas: ignore if R-TS(X) ≤ TS(T) < W-TS(X)Thomas Write Rule — stale blind write
Pass if finish(Tᵢ) < start(Tⱼ)
or start(Tⱼ) < finish(Tᵢ) < validation(Tⱼ) ∧ WS(Tᵢ) ∩ RS(Tⱼ) = ∅		Optimistic validation of Tj against Ti

3.Differences That Are Easy to Mix Up

PairDistinction
2PL vs Strict 2PL2PL releases locks in a shrinking phase; strict 2PL holds every exclusive lock until commit.
Conflict vs view serializabilityConflict uses the acyclic precedence graph; view uses initial reads, read-from and final writes. View serializable but not conflict serializable happens only with blind writes.
Recoverable vs cascadelessRecoverable just orders the commits; cascadeless forbids reading any uncommitted value, so no cascade can start.
Wait-Die vs Wound-WaitWait-Die: older waits, younger dies. Wound-Wait: older wounds the younger holder, younger waits.
Basic TO vs Thomas Write RuleThomas ignores a stale blind write instead of aborting; the read rule is unchanged.
UNDO vs REDOUNDO (backward) restores old values of uncommitted transactions; REDO (forward) re-applies new values of committed ones.
Deferred vs immediate modificationDeferred writes only after commit (REDO only); immediate writes any time (UNDO then REDO).
Clustered vs secondary indexClustered: matching records are physically together (h + r/bf). Secondary: about one I/O per record (h + r).
MySQL vs Oracle on deadlockMySQL rolls back the whole victim transaction; Oracle rolls back only the failing statement.
MySQL vs Oracle on readersMySQL default REPEATABLE READ gives a snapshot; Oracle default READ COMMITTED gives statement-level reads. Oracle has no READ UNCOMMITTED.
FOR UPDATE NOWAIT vs SKIP LOCKEDNOWAIT fails immediately; SKIP LOCKED silently ignores locked rows and returns the rest.

4.Rules & Conditions Checklist

Optimization

  • Push single-relation selections; a mixed condition goes just above the join.
  • Turn products + equality selection into joins.
  • Join the most selective pair first.
  • Push projections to keep only needed attributes.
  • Function-wrapped columns are not sargable.

Concurrency

  • Read/read never conflicts.
  • Acyclic precedence graph ⇔ conflict serializable.
  • Strict ⇒ cascadeless ⇒ recoverable.
  • S/S compatible; S/X and X/X block.
  • Lock point = end of the growing phase.
  • Deadlock ⇔ cycle in the wait-for graph.

Recovery

  • UNDO backward, REDO forward.
  • Commit before checkpoint → ignore.
  • Abort record → ignore.
  • Scan from the earliest start of a checkpoint-active transaction.
  • UNDO/REDO write absolute values (idempotent).
  • Shadow paging: lowest free location; commit frees the replaced ones.

Transactions

  • DDL commits implicitly.
  • A failed statement does not end the transaction.
  • AUTO_INCREMENT / identity values are not rolled back.
  • Re-issuing SAVEPOINT with the same name moves it.

5.Frequently Confusing Points

Traps the source flags explicitly
  1. Index nested loop is not automatically fastest. With unclustered matches it cost 301,250 against BNL's 76,250 in U3-A-07.
  2. A clustering column order matters. idx_ds(dept_id, salary) beat idx_sd(salary, dept_id) by about 10× in U3-A-09.
  3. Oracle needs IS NOT NULL before an index can serve an ordered scan on a nullable column (U3-A-15).
  4. REPEATABLE READ still shows a phantom on a locking read. The snapshot count stays 5000 while FOR SHARE returns 5001 (U3-C-20).
  5. MySQL and Oracle roll back different amounts on deadlock. Whole transaction vs single statement (U3-C-19).
  6. UNDO run forward gives the wrong value. A ends at 2 instead of 1 in U3-D-26.
  7. REDO run out of order gives the wrong value. P2 ends at 180 instead of 170 in U3-D-21.
  8. A committed transaction can still be undone indirectly. U3-D-19 shows T2's committed B derived from rolled-back A.
  9. A gap in the identity sequence is not an atomicity failure (U3-B-12).

7.Accuracy Notes & Curation Summary

Honesty note on execution (from the source audit)

The source states plainly that no MySQL or Oracle instance was available when it was written: every solution is hand-checked, and every “expected” plan, lock or log output is a description rather than a captured result. No SQL in this guide has been executed or tested here either. Run each exercise once; where an EXPLAIN or lock output differs from the description, trust your database.

What was retained

  • All four sections (A, B, C, D) with at least one worked example per distinct concept.
  • All formulas and cost models: block counts, selectivity, BNL and INL costs, access-path costs and break-even, TO/Thomas/OCC rules, recovery and checkpoint rules, shadow-paging rules.
  • The corrected U3-C-19 solution (MySQL rolls back the whole victim transaction; Oracle only the failing statement) — the source explicitly flags its earlier wording as wrong.
  • Platform-specific caveats: Oracle IS NOT NULL for ordered index scans, Oracle's FOR UPDATE + row-limiting restriction, MySQL gap locking, deadlock rollback scope, autocommit.
  • Every numbered table, recovery trace and shadow-paging snapshot for the selected questions.

What was consolidated or excluded

  • Setup scripts (u3_dept, u3_emp, u3_account, …) are not reproduced; the guide references the tables by name and states the assumed starting values instead.
  • Batch status reports, progress notes and conversational transitions from the four batches are removed.
  • Duplicate questions testing the same concept are collapsed into one worked example with a “Related” pointer to the parallel question (for example C-02 ↔ C-24, C-05 ↔ C-06 ↔ C-25, C-15 ↔ C-28, C-17 ↔ C-29, D-07/D-08/D-27).
  • The 40-question coverage matrix is summarised rather than reproduced row by row; its per-topic counts (A = 16, B = 12, C = 31, D = 27, 86 total, 30 executable) are preserved in the source.
  • Repeated expected outputs for the same pattern (for example the reset balances) are stated once.
  • Trivially similar variations that introduce no new concept were omitted, but no topic was dropped.

Source inconsistencies and open items requiring attention

ItemStatus / action
U3-C-19 final-balance wordingThe source admits the original paragraph was muddled and supplies a correction, which is used here. Note the Oracle branch depends on whether the erroring session issues ROLLBACK (102 = 4900) or COMMIT (102 = 4800).
Timestamp-ordering on-rampThe source notes C-15, C-16, C-22 and C-28 are all Level 4 with no Level 1–2 warm-up; it suggests hand-simplifying C-15 to two transactions first.
Shadow pagingFour questions, all manual — inherent, since neither platform exposes it.
Two-phase lockingManual simulations only (plus real-lock observation in C-10 and C-30); neither engine exposes a plain 2PL scheduler.
FreeSQL worksheetThe source could not verify support for DBMS_XPLAN, DBMS_STATS, SET AUTOCOMMIT or two simultaneous sessions. Use a local Oracle instance if a two-session exercise will not run there.
Parts 1 and 2The source never saw them, so the ID format, platform labels and the u3_ table prefix are its own conventions, not necessarily the university's. Match them before reuse.
Version dependenciesMySQL needs 8.0.16+ for enforced CHECK, 8.0.18+ for EXPLAIN ANALYZE; Oracle needs 12c+ for identity columns and FETCH FIRST.
Final check before an assessment

Reset the tables, then re-run one executable question from each section. If any expected output differs from what you see, record the question ID and the actual output — that is the fastest way to find whether the exercise or your environment needs adjusting.
